## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-juan Táng-era Chán lay-master's *yǔlù*, X69 n1336. Non-commentary; *commentedTextid* omitted.

[Páng Yùn](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BE%90%E8%98%8A) 龐蘊 (*hào* Dàoxuán 道玄; c. 740–808): the archetypal Chinese Chán lay practitioner. Reportedly cast his entire family wealth into the river to free himself of attachment, then lived a family life of manual labour (weaving bamboo baskets) while sustaining serious Chán practice with his wife and his daughter [Língzhào](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%88%E7%85%A7) 靈照. Páng trained under [Shítóu Xīqiān](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B8%8C%E9%81%B7) 石頭希遷, then with [Mǎzǔ Dàoyī](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E4%B8%80) 馬祖道一 (see [KR6q0267](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0267)). His deathbed *gāozuò* 高座 encounter with his daughter Língzhào has been one of the most-cited Chán stories throughout the tradition.

Compiler [Yú Dí](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BA%8E%E9%A0%94) 于頔: Táng scholar-official; lay patron of Páng Yùn. Lifedates approximately contemporary with Páng.

The Páng Yùn corpus is a foundational source for the ideal of serious lay Chán practice that has continued through the tradition — directly invoked by later lay-*yǔlù* such as [Xú Chāngzhì](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%90%E6%98%8C%E6%B2%BB)'s *Wúyī dàorén lù* [KR6q0192](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0192) in the late Míng.

Dating: *notBefore* c. 790 (Páng's mature teaching-years); *notAfter* c. 830 (Yú Dí's compilation-horizon in the early 9th century).
